journey.title: Opt out of reminders with the keyboard after choosing Text message
journey.goal: Arrowing from Text message to the opt-out answer hides the mobile number field that no longer applies

functionalJourney.goal: Choosing Email then Text message shows only the mobile number field

plan.root_cause: The radios component only updates conditional visibility on mouse click events. Keyboard navigation via ArrowDown changes the checked state of radio buttons but does not trigger the update, causing conditional fields to remain visible when they should be hidden.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a 'change' event listener to the radios module that invokes the same attribute update logic as the click handler. This ensures that any change in radio selection—whether via mouse, keyboard, or assistive technology—updates aria-expanded and toggles the visibility of associated conditional content.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate between radio options using arrow keys and see conditional fields show/hide appropriately, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Both click and change events may fire for the same interaction, but setAttributes is idempotent, so no adverse effect.
The handler only processes inputs with type radio and an aria-controls attribute, preventing unintended side effects on other form fields.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the Email radio to the Text message radio shows the mobile number field.
Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the Text message radio to the Opt‑out radio hides the mobile number field.
Verify that clicking a radio with mouse still updates the conditional content correctly.
Verify that pressing Space on a focused radio updates the conditional content.
Ensure no JavaScript errors are thrown in the console during these interactions.

plan.root_cause: The radios component only listens for 'click' events on its module element. Keyboard navigation (ArrowDown) changes the checked radio via native browser behavior, which fires a 'change' event on the radio input but not a 'click' event. Since the two radio groups (channel-radios and optout-radios) are separate modules but share the same 'name' attribute, selecting the opt-out radio in one module unchecks the text-message radio in the other module without the first module receiving any event, so its conditional field remains visible.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a document-level 'change' event listener in each Radios instance that filters for radio inputs sharing any name used by that instance's radios. When such a change occurs, invoke the existing handleClick logic to update all conditional reveals in that module. This ensures keyboard, mouse, and assistive-tech selections all update visibility correctly, even across module boundaries.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate between all radio options using arrow keys and see conditional fields show/hide appropriately across module boundaries, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Both click and change events may fire for the same interaction, but setAttributes is idempotent, so no adverse effect.
Multiple Radios instances on the same page will each add a document change listener; they filter by name so only relevant changes trigger handleClick.
The handler only processes inputs with type radio and an aria-controls attribute, preventing unintended side effects on other form fields.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the Email radio to the Text message radio shows the mobile number field.
Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the Text message radio to the Opt‑out radio hides the mobile number field.
Verify that clicking a radio with mouse still updates the conditional content correctly.
Verify that pressing Space on a focused radio updates the conditional content.
Ensure no JavaScript errors are thrown in the console during these interactions.
